title: In Rust every identity draw samples a texture or a modelled asset's own
note: What the facet exists to build is a textured Material or a modelled GLB, and every texture it binds is compressed (no assetIssues).
intent: Whatever the facet exists to build must not be flat colour. Three answers pass: a Material with a base texture (and its normal and roughness maps) from a CC0 set, a GLB whose own materials carry textures (modelled in Local Blender or fetched), or a decal laid on a textured surface. Read state().__render.textures after a capture: each texture the frame bound is named with its kind (color, data, normal) and a compressed family; give a loose image a [[texture]] row in genex.toml so it ships compressed, and keep __render.assetIssues absent.

check.note: The last frame bound at least three textures and the renderer names no asset issue (an uncompressed or refused texture).

port: The facet that owns a surface owns its Material and its CC0 set; a shared Material lives in the world, made once in on_reset.

evidence.note: __render.textures names every bound texture with its kind and family; __render.assetIssues names what to fix.
The three.js recipe materials.mapped-identity-tags, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
